title: Calendar-as-Code: automated launch calendar & guardrail enforcement
creator: Sofia Nguyen
description:
Problem: coordinating cross-service launches (runtime, console, API) today requires manual calendar updates, ad-hoc Slack approvals, and ad-hoc capacity reservation emails. This leads to missed conflicts, manual overruns, and last-minute rollbacks.

Proposal: implement a calendar-as-code system (YAML manifests checked into a single repo) that powers: 1) a canonical launch calendar in the Redwood Console, 2) CI checks that validate guardrails (blackout windows, required owners, capacity reservations), and 3) an API endpoint teams can use to programmatically reserve capacity and request blackout exemptions. The system will also surface conflicts and automatically create or update Linear parent tickets for cross-team orchestration.

Scope: MVP covers runtime, console, and API product launches; integrations with Dedicated capacity reservations and with our internal calendar (Google Calendar) sync; enforcement checks in CI; a small Console UI for launch owners to view and request changes. Does not include on-prem airgap flows (will be follow-up).
acceptance_criteria: Canonical calendar manifest format (YAML schema) defined and documented in Confluence: example manifests for runtime, console, api launches
CI validation check prevents merge of manifest that violates blackout windows or missing owners
Console embeds canonical calendar and shows conflict overlays with per-launch metadata (owners, capacity reservations, rollback owners)
API endpoint /launches accepts manifest POST and returns reservation id; success creates Linear parent orchestration ticket
Integration with Dedicated capacity allocator: reservation request creates pending reservation and notifies infra on-call
Basic e2e playbook documented and validated in dry-run (internal launch) with two teams completing flow
Telemetry: number of conflicts detected and time-to-resolve tracked in release dashboard
